tags.chapter_name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

question.text: The first and second ionisation enthalpies of a metal are <math><mn>496</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4560</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, respectively. How many moles of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></math> respectively, will be needed to react completely with <math><mn>1</mn></math> mole of the metal hydroxide?

solution.text:
Ionization Enthalpy values indicate that the metal belongs to Ist group, since the second ionization enthalpy is very high.
(Q - only one valence electron)
Metal hydroxide will be of the type, MOH.

MOH 1 mol + HCl 1 mol →MCl+ H 2 O

MOH+ 1 2 H 2 SO 4 → 1 2 M 2 SO 4 + H 2 O

(1mol) 1 2 mol So, one mole of HCl is required to react with one mole of MOH.

So, 1 2 mole of H 2 SO 4  is required to react with one mole of MOH.
